description: Wire the ranged fields into the modded-mob AI so a hostile modded mob with ranged_damage > 0 fires a projectile at a visible player within ranged_range, reusing the EXISTING base arrow path (MobEvent -> spawn_arrow -> Arrow::fly -> host-side damage -> Msg::Mobs replication). This stays host-authoritative and deterministic (sim dt + the seeded Rng already threaded into Mob::update, mirroring the Rattler). The projectile reuses the base Pointy Stick / arrow sprite for v1. Depends on FEAT-002.
steps: DESIGN (apply exactly): The modded ranged attack must honor the configured ranged_damage, but the existing spawn_arrow HARDCODES 3.0 for Rattler shots (shooter=None). So add a damage-carrying event rather than overloading the base Shoot. In src/entity.rs MobEvent enum (~line 604) add a new variant `ShootMod(Vec3, Vec3, f32)` with a doc comment '/// A modded mob fired a projectile: (from, velocity, damage).'. Do NOT change the existing `Shoot(Vec3, Vec3)` variant (base mobs keep using it).

In src/game.rs, where MobEvent is matched (~line 2587, the `MobEvent::Shoot(from, vel) => self.spawn_arrow(from, vel, None)` line), add an arm `MobEvent::ShootMod(from, vel, dmg) => self.spawn_arrow_dmg(from, vel, dmg),`. Add a small helper `spawn_arrow_dmg(&mut self, pos: Vec3, vel: Vec3, damage: f32)` next to spawn_arrow (~line 1369) that does exactly what spawn_arrow does for a mob shot (Arrow::new(pos, vel, None, damage), push, Sfx::Twang, cap at 200) but takes the damage explicitly. Keep spawn_arrow unchanged for base mobs. (The host-side hit resolution in update_arrows already reads a.damage and applies self.rules.difficulty.mob_damage(a.damage) + hurt_player_from + knockback for shooter==None, and hurt_peer for peers, so NO change is needed there and the modded damage flows through automatically.)

In src/entity.rs Mob::update, in the `MobKind::Modded(_) =>` arm (~line 1342), extend the logic. Resolve the def once (it is already fetched for melee). Compute whether ranged is enabled: `let ranged = def.hostile && def.ranged_damage > 0.0`. The mob should pursue when the player is visible and within max(aggro_range, ranged_range) if ranged, else aggro_range (so a ranged-only mob still approaches/tracks). Decide melee-vs-ranged by distance using the SHARED self.attack_cd timer (already decremented by dt at the top of update): (a) if melee is enabled (attack_damage>0) AND flat distance < attack_reach AND vertical offset < 1.6 AND attack_cd<=0 -> melee (push HurtPlayer(attack_damage, "was mauled by a monster"); attack_cd = attack_cooldown) EXACTLY as today; (b) ELSE if ranged is enabled AND player_visible AND flat distance < ranged_range AND attack_cd<=0 -> raycast a clear shot like the Rattler: `let eye = self.eye(); let aim = player - eye; let clear = world.raycast(eye, aim.normalize_or_zero(), aim.length()).is_none();` and if clear, push `MobEvent::ShootMod(eye + aim.normalize_or_zero() * 0.5, aim.normalize_or_zero() * def.projectile_speed + Vec3::Y * aim.length() * 0.42, def.ranged_damage)` then set `self.attack_cd = def.ranged_cooldown;`. This means: MELEE up close, RANGED at distance; melee takes priority inside attack_reach. Keep `want = Some((face, 2.3 * def.speed))` for the chase while hostile. Document this melee-vs-ranged precedence in a code comment. A mob with ranged_damage==0 behaves EXACTLY as the current melee/passive code (no new branch taken).

Determinism note to honor: use ONLY the passed-in sim dt and the seeded `rng` already in scope for any jitter; do not read wall-clock and do not introduce new RNG. The Rattler sets attack_cd = rng.range(1.6,2.6); for the modded mob use the deterministic configured def.ranged_cooldown directly (no extra randomness) so cadence is exactly data-driven and reproducible. (If you add any jitter, it MUST use the in-scope seeded rng.)

Confirm every MobKind match that must stay exhaustive still compiles: the new MobEvent::ShootMod only adds variants to the MobEvent match sites. Grep for `MobEvent::` match arms (game.rs ~2560-2592 and any client-side no-op handler) and add the ShootMod arm wherever MobEvent is matched exhaustively. The client never runs mob AI (host-authoritative), so ShootMod is only produced host-side and only needs handling in the host event loop in game.rs; verify there is no other exhaustive match on MobEvent that now fails to compile.

Add regression tests in src/game.rs mirroring bows_shoot_mobs_and_rattlers_shoot_back (~line 5043) and in src/entity.rs mirroring the modded-melee tests (~line 2389+). At minimum: (1) a hostile modded mob with ranged_damage>0 placed within ranged_range of the player, with clear line of sight, after several update_entities(dt) ticks has spawned at least one arrow and reduced the player's health (host-side), and it fires on the configured ranged_cooldown cadence (e.g. assert it does NOT fire again until cooldown elapses). (2) ranged OFF by default: a modded mob with no ranged fields never spawns an arrow and never ranged-damages the player. (3) a melee-only modded mob (attack_damage>0, ranged_damage=0) still only melees and spawns no arrows. (4) at the entity level (no full game), assert the Modded arm pushes a ShootMod event when beyond attack_reach but within ranged_range with the player visible, and a HurtPlayer (not ShootMod) when within attack_reach. Reuse the existing with_mods/arena/alloc_mob/hurt_hits test helpers. Keep seeds fixed for determinism.
Run `cargo test --no-default-features` and `cargo clippy --no-default-features --all-targets`; fix all warnings. Commit on branch modded-mob-ranged-attacks.
acceptance_criteria: A hostile modded mob with ranged_damage>0 within ranged_range and clear LoS spawns an Arrow host-side and damages the player, on the ranged_cooldown cadence, deterministically
Projectile flight, damage, and replication reuse the existing Arrow / spawn_arrow / update_arrows / Msg::Mobs path; NO new client-trusted projectile system and NO wire or save format change
Melee-vs-ranged interaction is: melee inside attack_reach, ranged beyond it within ranged_range; documented in a code comment
ranged_damage==0 (default) mobs are behaviorally identical to the current melee/passive code; base mobs untouched
New tests cover: ranged fires+damages at cadence, ranged OFF by default, melee-only still only melees, and the event-level distance branching
cargo test --no-default-features passes (>= 255 + new tests); cargo clippy --no-default-features --all-targets zero warnings; Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock unchanged
findings: Implemented AI wiring only (docs/example mod deferred to a later feature, as instructed). Added MobEvent::ShootMod(Vec3, Vec3, f32) in src/entity.rs (base Shoot untouched). In src/game.rs added the ShootMod match arm plus spawn_arrow_dmg (mirrors spawn_arrow's shooter==None path but takes explicit damage; spawn_arrow unchanged). update_arrows needed no change - it already reads a.damage and applies difficulty scaling + hurt_player_from/knockback for shooter==None, so modded damage flows through. Extended the MobKind::Modded arm in Mob::update: ranged = hostile && ranged_damage>0; pursue within max(aggro_range, ranged_range) when ranged; melee takes priority inside attack_reach (unchanged), else fire ShootMod when within ranged_range, attack_cd<=0, and a world.raycast LoS is clear, setting attack_cd = ranged_cooldown (no jitter; deterministic). ranged_damage==0 mobs take no new branch and are behaviorally identical. The only exhaustive MobEvent match is in game.rs (~2598); hollow.rs uses matches!(..) so needed no change. Verification: cargo test --no-default-features = 260 passed (was 255; +5 incl FEAT-002's). cargo clippy --no-default-features --all-targets = zero warnings. Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock untouched. Added 4 regression tests (2 entity-level: distance branching ShootMod vs HurtPlayer + melee priority, ranged-off-by-default; 2 game-level: ranged fires+damages at cadence through the real arrow path, ranged-off and melee-only never spawn an arrow).
